newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS MARGINALLY LOWER, CROWN SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS MARGINALLY LOWER, CROWN SOFTER.

text.p: Long Swedish bond yields were marginally lower around midday on Thursday after edging off morning lows ahead of U.S. July consumer price figures at 1230 GMT, while the crown kept softening against the mark.

"Underlying sentiment is fairly negative," a trader said. "When bunds soften Swedish debt follows, but when bunds perform better we don't do anything. That shows there is some sell pressure in the market."
The six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.34 percent while the 10-year bond yield was one basis point lower at 6.59 percent.
Dealers expected some turmoil when U.S. figures were released.
The crown softened to 4.3550 against the mark from 4.3425 late on Wednesday and dealers saw it weakening further.
"I think we will see the range 4.34-4.37 to the mark today," one dealer said.
